verified.story_title: Koniag Advisory & Business Solutions wins $18M DOE SBIR/STTR support contract via 8(a) sole source
verified.summary: Koniag Advisory and Business Solutions LLC, a subsidiary of Koniag Government Services (an Alaska Native Corporation-affiliated company for Kodiak Archipelago shareholders), was awarded a five-year $18,023,062 contract by the Department of Energy to provide programmatic support for DOE's SBIR/STTR programs. Award date June 5, 2026; 8(a) sole-source, single bidder, contract ID 89303026CTT000007.
verified.why_it_matters: ANC 8(a) status unlocked the award through a civilian agency (DOE), channeling federal dollars to a Kodiak-connected Native corporation. 8(a) sole source is a preference channel, and the work is program support (back office), not the AI workloads themselves.
verified.industry_consequence: Federal services: Koniag Government Services secures an $18M, 5-year DOE revenue stream via 8(a) sole source. ANC 8(a) preference is the dominant channel putting federal AI-adjacent dollars into Alaska-owned entities, which is a concentration risk if the preference tightens.
verified.corrections: Use award ID 89303026CTT000007 and $18,023,062 (round to ~$18M). Candidate USAspending URL did not resolve; attribute award details to the federal contract record as reported June 5 (OrangeSlices). Koniag-gs page confirms entity identity only. Attribute carefully: 'a federal contract record reported June 5'.

verified.story_title: NSF TechAccess AI-Ready America Round 1 LOI closes June 16 — Alaska eligible for a $3M, 3-year AI workforce hub
verified.summary: NSF's TechAccess: AI-Ready America (NSF 26-508), a $168M to $224M initiative, funds one AI Coordination Hub per state/territory at $1M/yr for 3 years. Round 1 selects 10 hubs; mandatory LOI due June 16, 2026. Alaska is one of 56 eligible jurisdictions; the University of Alaska System is an eligible lead type.
verified.why_it_matters: Use-it-or-lose-it: missing the June 16 LOI defers Alaska to Round 2 (Dec 15, 2026) while 10 states build hubs first.
verified.industry_consequence: Higher ed/workforce: University of Alaska System (or an AWIB consortium) must decide by June 16, 2026 whether to file an LOI for a $3M, 3-year NSF AI hub.
verified.corrections: Use '$168M to $224M', not a flat $224M. DOL source dropped (403). GrantedAI is a blog; hedge any GrantedAI-specific detail. Do NOT assert a confirmed Alaska filing. The $3M is $1M/yr x 3yr per hub.

verified.story_title: AFA Council 30 (Alaska Airlines flight attendants) enters national AI-labor fight as Great American AI Act drops
verified.summary: LeiLauni Scheideman, president of AFA Council 30 representing Anchorage-based Alaska Airlines flight attendants, published an ADN op-ed June 1, 2026 opposing federal preemption of state AI worker protections, citing AI monitoring of flight attendants. On June 4 the bipartisan Great American AI Act discussion draft proposed a three-year preemption of state AI laws; AFA-CWA and AFT issued a joint statement opposing it.
verified.why_it_matters: Alaska has no enacted AI labor law; a federal preemption would lock the legislature out of passing AI workplace guardrails for three years as Alaska Airlines deepens AI deployment.
verified.industry_consequence: Aviation-labor: AFA Council 30 (Anchorage) faces a closing window; if the Great American AI Act advances, Alaska loses the ability to enact AI workplace-monitoring protections through about 2028.
verified.corrections: GAAIA preemption itself was covered in prior weeks; the NEW element is the AFA/aviation-labor angle. Verified joint-statement quote available ('Our response to the Great American AI Act is simple: Hard no.') but quote not required. Roll Call confirms the 3-year preemption; Scheideman op-ed is the Alaska link.

verified.story_title: Glenfarne reveals $44.5B to $55B Alaska LNG cost range; June 19 special-session deadline
verified.summary: During the LNG special session Glenfarne disclosed June 3-4 the project will cost $44.5B to $54.5B (Alaska Public Media, June 4); ADN reported June 6 the high end updated to $55B. Senate Finance co-chair Bert Stedman called it low, estimating $62B to $65B. The tax bill must pass by June 19.
verified.why_it_matters: Alaska LNG is the only large-scale gas answer to the Railbelt Cook Inlet shortage that Chugach and GVEA cite when declining large data-center loads; the Governor has pitched it as the AI data-center energy backbone.
verified.industry_consequence: Energy/AI infra: the June 19 vote gates whether grid-connected Railbelt data centers ever pencil; the updated cost resets power economics under every gigawatt pitch.
verified.corrections: Covered in prior weeks; use only as a one-line stakes/context beat. Use '$44.5B to $55B' range; attribute Stedman's $62B-$65B as his estimate.

verified.story_title: Alaska DNR comment period on Stak Energy $500M North Slope AI data-center land lease closes June 15
verified.summary: DNR issued a preliminary best-interest finding supporting a 50-year state land lease to Stak Energy for a gas-powered data center near Deadhorse, about one square mile, up to 3GW, $500M, no gas supply agreement secured. Public comment closes June 15, 2026.
verified.why_it_matters: June 15 comment close is an in-window action-forcing date; finalization could encumber state land at scale with no energy source secured.
verified.industry_consequence: Oil & gas / digital infra: DNR may finalize a 50-year lease after June 15; North Slope gas producers must signal supply interest or opposition before the comment window closes.
verified.corrections: STRIP '715-acre'; use 'about one square mile'. Both sources pre-window; June 15 comment close is the in-window hook. Use as one-line supporting beat only.
